units.text: Bright-eyed Muses, tell of the Tyndaridae, the
of neat-ankled Leda, Castor the tamer
of horses, and blameless Polydeuces. When Leda
had lain with the dark-clouded Son of Cronos,
she bare them beneath the peak of the great
hill Taygetus, — children who are deliverers of men on earth
and of swift-going ships when stormy gales rage over the ruthless sea. Then the
shipmen call upon the sons of great Zeus
with vows of white lambs, going to the
forepart of the prow; but the strong wind and the waves of the sea
lay the ship under water, until suddenly these two are
seen darting through the air on tawny wings.
Forthwith they allay the blasts of the cruel winds
and still the waves upon the surface of the white sea:
fair signs are they and deliverance from toil. And when the
shipmen see them they are glad and have
rest from their pain and labour. Hail, Tyndaridae,
riders upon swift horses! Now I will remember you and another song also.
